items.en: Explain what "total rewards" means to a new employee.
items.vi: Giải thích "tổng đãi ngộ" cho nhân viên mới.
hints: Total rewards is everything an employee receives in exchange for their work.
It includes pay, but also benefits, well-being, recognition and development.
Some parts are financial, others are non-financial.
Give one example of a non-cash reward that people often forget.
items.opener: When people hear "rewards", they usually think of salary, but total rewards is much broader than that.

items.en: Describe the five parts of the total rewards model.
items.vi: Mô tả 5 cấu phần của mô hình tổng đãi ngộ.
hints: Compensation: fixed and variable pay.
Benefits: insurance, leave and other protection.
Well-being: physical, mental and financial health.
Performance and recognition, plus development and career opportunities.
Explain why a company needs all five, not just pay.
items.opener: The total rewards model has five components, and I'll go through them one by one.

items.en: Explain the three main goals of a rewards programme.
items.vi: Giải thích ba mục tiêu chính của chương trình đãi ngộ.
hints: Attract: bring the right people into the company.
Motivate: encourage people to perform and grow.
Retain: keep the people the company cannot afford to lose.
Give an example of a reward that supports each goal.
items.opener: Every rewards programme should answer one question: does it help us attract, motivate or retain the right people?

items.en: What is variable pay, and how is it different from fixed pay?
items.vi: Lương biến đổi là gì, khác lương cố định thế nào?
hints: Fixed pay is guaranteed: base salary and fixed allowances.
Variable pay depends on results: bonuses, commission, incentives.
Variable pay must be earned again every period.
It shares risk between the company and the employee.
items.opener: The simplest way to explain the difference is this: fixed pay rewards the job, and variable pay rewards results.

items.en: Explain what a compensation philosophy is and why it matters.
items.vi: Giải thích triết lý đãi ngộ là gì và vì sao quan trọng.
hints: It's a set of principles that explains why and how we pay people.
It covers market position, pay mix and what we reward.
It helps managers make consistent decisions.
It makes pay easier to communicate and defend.
items.opener: A compensation philosophy is like a compass: it doesn't give you every answer, but it shows you the direction.

items.en: What is a total rewards statement, and why send one?
items.vi: Bảng tổng đãi ngộ là gì, vì sao nên gửi cho nhân viên?
hints: It's a personal document that shows the full value of an employee's package.
It includes pay, bonus, insurance, leave and training.
Most employees underestimate what the company spends on them.
It improves understanding and can support retention.
items.opener: Most employees only look at their payslip, so they see just part of the picture.

items.en: Explain the lead-lag pay policy.
items.vi: Giải thích chính sách lương dẫn – chậm.
hints: The market moves during the year, but our salaries change only once.
With lead-lag, we set pay at the market level expected in the middle of the year.
So we lead the market in the first half and lag in the second half.
On average, we stay in line with the market over the year.
useful: in the first half of the year
items.opener: Salaries are usually adjusted once a year, but the market doesn't stand still, and that's where lead-lag comes in.

items.en: What is a pay grade?
items.vi: Ngạch lương là gì?
hints: A pay grade is a group of jobs with similar value to the company.
Each grade has its own salary range.
Jobs in the same grade can be very different, like an accountant and an IT specialist.
Grades make pay decisions more consistent.
items.opener: A pay grade is basically a box: we put jobs of similar value into the same box and give that box a salary range.

items.en: Explain what the midpoint of a salary range represents.
items.vi: Giải thích điểm giữa của dải lương thể hiện điều gì.
hints: The midpoint is the middle of the range between minimum and maximum.
It is usually linked to the market rate we want to pay.
It represents pay for a fully competent, experienced person.
New hires usually start below it; top performers can go above it.
items.opener: If you remember only one number in a salary range, it should be the midpoint.

items.en: What is a pay range, and how do we measure its width?
items.vi: Dải lương là gì và đo độ rộng thế nào?
hints: A pay range has a minimum, a midpoint and a maximum.
Range spread is the difference between max and min, as a percentage of the minimum.
Junior roles have narrower ranges; senior roles have wider ones.
A wider range leaves more room for growth inside the job.
items.opener: A pay range tells us the lowest and the highest we're willing to pay for a job.

items.en: Explain range overlap between two grades.
items.vi: Giải thích độ chồng lấn giữa hai ngạch.
hints: Overlap is the part of a lower grade's range that is shared with the next grade.
Some overlap is healthy: an experienced senior can earn as much as a new manager.
Too much overlap makes promotions feel meaningless.
Too little overlap creates very big jumps at promotion.
items.opener: When two salary ranges overlap, it means some people in the lower grade can earn the same as people in the grade above.

items.en: What is broadbanding, and when does it make sense?
items.vi: Dải lương rộng là gì, khi nào nên dùng?
hints: Broadbanding combines many narrow grades into a few wide bands.
It gives managers more flexibility and supports a flatter organisation.
It suits companies that reward skills and career growth.
Risks: less control over costs and less structure for managers.
items.opener: Broadbanding means replacing many small grades with a handful of very wide bands.

items.en: Explain gainsharing and how it differs from profit sharing.
items.vi: Giải thích gainsharing và khác chia lợi nhuận thế nào.
hints: Gainsharing rewards a group for improving productivity or cutting costs.
The money comes from the savings the team creates.
Profit sharing is based on the profit of the whole company.
Gainsharing has a clearer line of sight for employees.
items.opener: Gainsharing and profit sharing sound similar, but they reward very different things.

items.en: What is profit sharing?
items.vi: Chia sẻ lợi nhuận là gì?
hints: Profit sharing gives employees part of the company's profit.
It is usually paid once a year after the results are confirmed.
It builds a sense of ownership and team spirit.
But individuals may feel they can't influence the result.
items.opener: Profit sharing is a simple idea: when the company does well, everyone gets a piece of the success.

items.en: Compare short-term and long-term incentives.
items.vi: So sánh khuyến khích ngắn hạn và dài hạn.
hints: Short-term incentives reward results within one year, like annual bonuses.
Long-term incentives reward results over three to five years.
Long-term incentives are often shares, options or deferred cash.
They help retain senior people and align them with shareholders.
items.opener: The main difference between short-term and long-term incentives is the time horizon.

items.en: Explain compa-ratio to a line manager.
items.vi: Giải thích compa-ratio cho quản lý trực tiếp.
hints: Compa-ratio is an employee's salary divided by the midpoint of their range.
One point zero means they are paid exactly at the midpoint.
Below one is normal for new or developing people.
Above one is normal for very experienced, high-performing people.
items.opener: Compa-ratio is one of the simplest numbers in C&B, and it tells you a lot about where someone is paid.

items.en: What is range penetration?
items.vi: Mức thâm nhập dải lương là gì?
hints: It shows how far an employee has moved through their range.
Zero percent is at the minimum; one hundred percent is at the maximum.
Formula: salary minus minimum, divided by maximum minus minimum.
It's useful when ranges are not symmetrical or very wide.
items.opener: Range penetration answers a simple question: how far along the range has this person travelled?

items.en: Explain the difference between compa-ratio and market index.
items.vi: Phân biệt compa-ratio và market index.
hints: Compa-ratio compares pay with our own midpoint: it's internal.
Market index compares pay with the market rate: it's external.
If our structure is behind the market, the two numbers will differ.
Using both gives a more complete picture.
useful: the two numbers can tell different stories
let me give you an example
items.opener: Compa-ratio and market index look alike, but they compare pay against two different things.

items.en: What is a red-circle employee, and how do you manage it?
items.vi: Nhân viên "vòng tròn đỏ" là gì, xử lý thế nào?
hints: A red-circle employee is paid above the maximum of their range.
Causes: long service, past negotiations or no benchmarking.
Common approach: no base increase until the range catches up.
Options: lump-sum payments, re-evaluating the job or a promotion.
items.opener: A red-circle employee is someone whose salary is higher than the top of their range.

items.en: What is a green-circle employee?
items.vi: Nhân viên "vòng tròn xanh" là gì?
hints: A green-circle employee is paid below the minimum of their range.
It can happen with new hires, after ranges move up, or by mistake.
Usually we bring them up to the minimum quickly.
If they're still learning the job, we agree a plan to get there.
items.opener: A green-circle employee is the opposite of a red-circle one: they're paid below the bottom of the range.

items.en: Explain pay compression and how to fix it.
items.vi: Giải thích nén lương và cách khắc phục.
hints: Compression is when pay differences between levels or people become too small.
Example: new hires earn almost as much as experienced staff.
Causes: hot market, small merit budgets, small grade gaps.
Fixes: equity adjustments, reviewing hiring rates and redesigning the structure.
useful: new hires earn almost as much as
items.opener: Pay compression happens quietly, and many companies notice it only when experienced people start to leave.

items.en: Explain the 25th, 50th and 75th percentiles in a salary survey.
items.vi: Giải thích phân vị 25, 50, 75 trong khảo sát lương.
hints: Percentiles show where a salary sits compared with the whole market.
At the 50th percentile, half the market pays more and half pays less.
The 75th percentile is a higher, more competitive level.
Which one we use depends on our pay philosophy.
items.opener: Imagine lining up one hundred companies from the lowest to the highest salary.

items.en: What is the market pricing approach?
items.vi: Định giá theo thị trường là gì?
hints: We value jobs mainly by what the external market pays.
First we match our jobs to survey jobs, then we look at the market data.
It's fast and keeps us competitive.
But it can weaken internal equity if the market is unusual.
items.opener: With market pricing, the market tells us how much a job is worth.

items.en: Explain the point factor method of job evaluation.
items.vi: Giải thích phương pháp chấm điểm yếu tố.
hints: We choose compensable factors, such as skill, effort, responsibility and working conditions.
Each factor has levels and points.
Each job gets a total score, and scores are grouped into grades.
It's systematic and easy to defend, but it takes time.
items.opener: The point factor method works a bit like a scoring system in an exam.

items.en: What is pay mix, and why does it differ by role?
items.vi: Pay mix là gì, vì sao khác nhau theo vai trò?
hints: Pay mix is the split between fixed pay and target variable pay.
Sales roles may have a 60/40 mix; support roles maybe 90/10.
The more a role can influence results, the more variable pay it has.
The mix shapes behaviour and risk.
items.opener: Two jobs can have the same total target pay but a very different pay mix.

items.en: Explain threshold, target and cap in a bonus plan.
items.vi: Giải thích ngưỡng, mục tiêu và trần trong kế hoạch thưởng.
hints: The threshold is the minimum performance before any bonus is paid, often 70 to 80 percent.
The target is the expected level, which pays 100 percent of the bonus.
The cap is the maximum payout, often 150 to 200 percent.
Together, they define the payout curve.
useful: the reason for a cap is
items.opener: Every well-designed bonus plan has three key points: threshold, target and cap.

items.en: What are malus and clawback?
items.vi: Malus và clawback là gì?
hints: Malus reduces or cancels a bonus before it is paid.
Clawback recovers a bonus that has already been paid.
Both are used when serious misconduct or errors are discovered.
They protect the company and encourage responsible behaviour.
items.opener: Malus and clawback sound technical, but the idea behind them is simple: rewards should be deserved.

items.en: Explain how a commission accelerator works.
items.vi: Giải thích hệ số gia tốc hoa hồng.
hints: An accelerator increases the commission rate above a certain level, usually quota.
It motivates top performers to keep selling.
A decelerator lowers the rate below a level.
It should be tested with past data to control the cost.
items.opener: An accelerator is a way of saying to sales people: the more you sell, the more each sale is worth.

items.en: Compare stock options and restricted stock units.
items.vi: So sánh quyền chọn cổ phiếu và RSU.
hints: Stock options give the right to buy shares at a fixed price.
They only have value if the share price rises above that price.
RSUs are shares given after a vesting period, so they usually keep some value.
Both are used to retain key people and align them with shareholders.
items.opener: Stock options and RSUs are both equity rewards, but the risk for the employee is quite different.

items.en: Why is job analysis the first step in building a pay system?
items.vi: Vì sao phân tích công việc là bước đầu khi xây hệ thống lương?
hints: Job analysis collects information about what a job involves.
It produces job descriptions and job specifications.
Without it, job evaluation and market matching are just guesses.
Sources: interviews, questionnaires, observation.
items.opener: You can't decide what a job is worth until you know what the job actually is.

items.en: Explain job architecture.
items.vi: Giải thích kiến trúc công việc.
hints: Job architecture organises all jobs into families, career tracks and levels.
Example: job family, then track such as professional or management, then level.
It links each job to a pay range and career path.
It makes career moves and pay decisions clearer.
items.opener: Job architecture is the framework that tells you where every job in the company sits.

items.en: What is a benchmark job?
items.vi: Công việc chuẩn (benchmark job) là gì?
hints: A benchmark job is a well-known job that exists in many companies.
It has a clear and stable description, so it's easy to match in surveys.
We use benchmark jobs as anchor points for the structure.
Other jobs can then be slotted around them.
items.opener: When we build a salary structure, we don't price every job; we start with benchmark jobs.

items.en: Explain what job evaluation is and why companies do it.
items.vi: Đánh giá công việc là gì, vì sao doanh nghiệp làm?
hints: Job evaluation compares jobs to decide their relative value.
It evaluates the job, not the person doing it.
The result is a job worth hierarchy, the basis of the grade structure.
It supports internal equity and fair pay decisions.
items.opener: Job evaluation is about one question: how important is this job compared with others in the company?

items.en: How does a merit increase work?
items.vi: Tăng lương theo thành tích vận hành thế nào?
hints: A merit increase is an annual increase to base pay based on performance.
It comes from a fixed merit budget, often a percentage of payroll.
It becomes part of salary permanently.
It only works if ratings really differentiate performance.
items.opener: A merit increase rewards past performance by increasing base salary for the future.

items.en: Explain how a merit matrix works.
items.vi: Giải thích ma trận tăng lương.
hints: A merit matrix combines performance rating and position in range.
Higher ratings get higher increases.
People low in the range get more than people high in the range, for the same rating.
Over time, people with the same performance move towards the same pay level.
items.opener: A merit matrix is a table that answers two questions at once: how well did you perform, and where are you paid today?

items.en: When do we use an equity or market adjustment?
items.vi: Khi nào dùng điều chỉnh công bằng hoặc điều chỉnh thị trường?
hints: An equity adjustment fixes unfair gaps inside the company.
A market adjustment brings pay up when it falls behind the market.
Both are separate from the normal merit increase.
They need clear evidence and a separate budget.
items.opener: Not every pay increase is about performance; sometimes we need to correct a gap.

items.en: Explain the 3P pay model.
items.vi: Giải thích mô hình lương 3P.
hints: P1, pay for position: the value of the job sets the range.
P2, pay for person: skills and competence decide where you sit in the range.
P3, pay for performance: results are rewarded through bonuses.
Together, they balance internal equity, market competitiveness and motivation.
items.opener: 3P is a popular model in Vietnam, and it answers three questions: what job do you do, how good are you at it, and what results do you deliver?

items.en: What is a calibration meeting, and why is it useful?
items.vi: Họp hiệu chỉnh xếp loại là gì, có ích gì?
hints: Managers meet to review and compare performance ratings across teams.
The goal is consistency: the same standard for everyone.
It reduces bias, such as managers who are too generous or too strict.
HR usually facilitates and asks for evidence.
items.opener: Without calibration, a "good" rating in one team can mean something very different in another team.

items.en: What makes an incentive plan effective?
items.vi: Điều gì làm kế hoạch khuyến khích hiệu quả?
hints: Line of sight: employees can see how their actions affect the result.
Few, clear measures that are cascaded from company goals.
A payout that is big enough to matter.
A performance culture where results really make a difference.
useful: if people can't see the link
items.opener: The best incentive plans are the ones employees can explain in one sentence.

items.en: Explain Herzberg's idea about pay and motivation.
items.vi: Giải thích quan điểm của Herzberg về lương và động lực.
hints: Herzberg separated hygiene factors from motivators.
Hygiene factors, like pay and conditions, prevent dissatisfaction.
Motivators, like achievement and recognition, create real motivation.
So fair pay is necessary, but it isn't enough on its own.
items.opener: One of the most useful ideas in rewards comes from Herzberg: money doesn't always motivate.

items.en: Explain to an employee why their payslip changed this month.
items.vi: Giải thích cho nhân viên vì sao phiếu lương tháng này thay đổi.
hints: Start by looking at the payslip together.
Name the change: a new allowance, overtime, a bonus or a deduction.
Explain the effect on tax or insurance.
Tell them what will happen next month.
useful: if you have any other questions
items.opener: Thanks for asking. Let's go through your payslip line by line.

items.en: Explain the annual salary review process to a new manager.
items.vi: Giải thích quy trình xét lương năm cho một quản lý mới.
hints: Timing: when the cycle starts and when decisions are final.
Inputs: performance ratings, position in range and the budget.
The manager's role: make proposals and explain them to the team.
Approval and communication steps.
items.opener: The salary review can feel complicated the first time, so let me give you the big picture.

items.en: How would you communicate a pay decision that an employee won't like?
items.vi: Bạn truyền đạt quyết định lương mà nhân viên sẽ không thích thế nào?
hints: Prepare the facts and the reasons before the meeting.
Deliver the message clearly and early in the conversation.
Listen and acknowledge their feelings.
Explain what they can do to change the outcome in the future.
useful: I want to be straightforward with you
items.opener: The worst thing you can do with bad news is hide it in the middle of a long explanation.

items.en: Should companies be open about salary ranges?
items.vi: Doanh nghiệp có nên công khai dải lương không?
hints: Benefits: trust, fairness and fewer rumours.
Risks: more questions and pressure on managers.
Preparation: clean structure and trained managers.
Give your own opinion with a reason.
items.opener: Pay transparency is one of the hottest topics in rewards right now, and I have mixed feelings about it.

items.en: Describe a benefit you would add at your company, and why.
items.vi: Mô tả một phúc lợi bạn muốn bổ sung ở công ty và lý do.
hints: Name the benefit.
Explain who would use it and why it matters to them.
Estimate the cost roughly.
Explain how it would help attract or keep people.
items.opener: If I could add one benefit tomorrow, it would be...

items.en: Describe your current job and your main responsibilities.
items.vi: Mô tả công việc hiện tại và trách nhiệm chính.
hints: Your job title and team.
Two or three main responsibilities.
Who you work with most.
What you like about the job.
useful: the part I enjoy most is
items.opener: I work as a C&B specialist in a team of five people.

items.en: Describe a typical working day.
items.vi: Mô tả một ngày làm việc điển hình.
hints: How your day starts.
The main tasks in the morning and afternoon.
Meetings and people you talk to.
How the day usually ends.
useful: by the end of the day
items.opener: My day usually starts with a cup of coffee and my inbox.

items.en: Talk about a project you're proud of.
items.vi: Kể về một dự án bạn tự hào.
hints: What the project was and why it was needed.
Your role in it.
A challenge you faced.
The result and what you learned.
items.opener: One project I'm really proud of is the new allowance policy we launched last year.

items.en: Describe the best quality of a manager you've worked with.
items.vi: Mô tả phẩm chất tốt nhất của một quản lý bạn từng làm cùng.
hints: Introduce the manager without using their name.
Name one quality.
Give a specific example.
Explain how it affected you.
useful: I try to do the same
items.opener: The best manager I've had was someone who always listened before she decided.

items.en: How do you handle stress at work?
items.vi: Bạn xử lý căng thẳng trong công việc thế nào?
hints: Describe what usually causes stress in your job.
One practical thing you do during the day.
One thing you do outside work.
How you ask for help when needed.
useful: the busiest time for me is
items.opener: Stress is part of the job in C&B, especially during payroll and salary review season.

items.en: Talk about a mistake you made at work and what you learned.
items.vi: Kể về một lỗi bạn mắc trong công việc và bài học.
hints: What happened, briefly.
How you discovered it.
What you did to fix it.
What you changed afterwards.
items.opener: Everyone makes mistakes, and one of mine taught me a lot about double-checking.

items.en: How do you prioritise when everything is urgent?
items.vi: Bạn sắp xếp ưu tiên thế nào khi mọi việc đều gấp?
hints: List all the tasks and deadlines.
Separate what is urgent from what is important.
Talk to stakeholders about realistic timing.
Ask your manager when priorities conflict.
items.opener: When everything is urgent, the first thing I do is stop and make a list.

items.en: What does work-life balance mean to you?
items.vi: Cân bằng công việc – cuộc sống với bạn là gì?
hints: Give your own definition.
Describe what you do after work.
Explain what makes balance hard in your job.
Say what companies can do to help.
items.opener: For me, work-life balance doesn't mean working less; it means having time for the people I love.

items.en: Do you prefer working from home or in the office?
items.vi: Bạn thích làm ở nhà hay ở văn phòng hơn?
hints: State your preference.
Give two reasons.
Mention one disadvantage.
Say what an ideal arrangement would be.
items.opener: Honestly, I like a mix of both, but if I had to choose...

items.en: Where do you see your career in five years?
items.vi: Bạn thấy sự nghiệp của mình ở đâu sau 5 năm?
hints: The role you want.
The skills you need to develop.
The steps you're taking now.
Why this goal matters to you.
useful: in five years, I'd like to
to get there, I need to
items.opener: In five years, I'd like to be leading a reward team.

items.en: What skills will HR professionals need in the future?
items.vi: Người làm nhân sự sẽ cần kỹ năng gì trong tương lai?
hints: Data and analytics skills.
Understanding the business, not just HR.
Communication and storytelling.
Adaptability as technology changes.
items.opener: HR is changing fast, and I think three skills will matter more than anything else.

items.en: How could artificial intelligence change HR work?
items.vi: AI có thể thay đổi công việc nhân sự thế nào?
hints: Tasks it can automate, like answering routine questions.
How it can help with analysis.
Risks: bias, privacy and wrong answers.
What humans will still need to do.
useful: keep a human in the loop
items.opener: AI won't replace HR, but HR people who use AI may replace those who don't.

items.en: Describe a colleague you learned a lot from.
items.vi: Mô tả một đồng nghiệp mà bạn học hỏi được nhiều.
hints: Who they are and how you worked together.
What they were good at.
One specific thing they taught you.
How you use it today.
items.opener: When I first joined the company, I sat next to someone who changed the way I work.

items.en: Give advice to someone starting their first job in HR.
items.vi: Lời khuyên cho người mới bắt đầu việc đầu tiên trong ngành nhân sự.
hints: Learn the basics of labour law and payroll.
Listen to employees and managers.
Be careful with confidential information.
Ask questions and find a mentor.
useful: my first piece of advice is
items.opener: If you're starting out in HR, here are three things I wish someone had told me.

items.en: How do you build good relationships with other departments?
items.vi: Bạn xây dựng quan hệ tốt với các phòng ban khác thế nào?
hints: Understand their goals and pressures.
Communicate early, not only when there's a problem.
Keep your promises and deadlines.
Give an example from your work.
items.opener: In C&B, we can't do anything alone, so relationships with other teams are essential.

items.en: What makes a good team?
items.vi: Điều gì tạo nên một đội nhóm tốt?
hints: Clear goals.
Trust and open communication.
People with different strengths.
An example of a good team you were in.
useful: the best team I've been in
items.opener: I think a good team is more than a group of good people.

items.en: How do you give feedback to a colleague?
items.vi: Bạn góp ý cho đồng nghiệp thế nào?
hints: Choose the right time and place.
Describe the behaviour, not the person.
Explain the impact.
Suggest a way forward and listen.
items.opener: Giving feedback to a peer can be harder than giving it to someone in your team.

items.en: Talk about a time you had to learn something quickly.
items.vi: Kể về lần bạn phải học điều gì đó thật nhanh.
hints: What you needed to learn and why.
How much time you had.
How you learned it.
The result.
items.opener: Last year, I had to learn a new payroll system in less than two weeks.

items.en: Give a short update on a project you're working on.
items.vi: Cập nhật ngắn về một dự án bạn đang làm.
hints: What the project is.
What's done.
What's next.
Any risks or help needed.
items.opener: Just a quick update on the benefits renewal project.

items.en: Present one key number from your work and explain it.
items.vi: Trình bày một con số quan trọng trong công việc và giải thích.
hints: State the number clearly.
Compare it with something: last year, the target or the market.
Explain why it changed.
Say what action is needed.
useful: the number I want to highlight is
what this means for us is
items.opener: The number I'd like you to remember today is eighteen percent.

items.en: Open a meeting: welcome people, state the purpose and the agenda.
items.vi: Mở đầu cuộc họp: chào, nêu mục đích và chương trình.
hints: Welcome and thank people.
State the purpose in one sentence.
Go through the agenda items.
Mention the time and how you'll take questions.
useful: the purpose of this meeting is
please save questions for the end
items.opener: Good morning, everyone, and thanks for joining.

items.en: Close a meeting: summarise and confirm next steps.
items.vi: Kết thúc cuộc họp: tóm tắt và xác nhận bước tiếp theo.
hints: Summarise the main decisions.
Confirm who does what and by when.
Mention the next meeting.
Thank people.
items.opener: We're almost out of time, so let me wrap up.

items.en: Disagree politely with a proposal in a meeting.
items.vi: Phản đối lịch sự một đề xuất trong cuộc họp.
hints: Acknowledge the good parts of the idea.
State your concern clearly.
Give a reason or data.
Suggest an alternative.
useful: I can see the benefits of
items.opener: I like the idea in principle, but I have one concern.

items.en: Persuade your manager to support a new idea.
items.vi: Thuyết phục quản lý ủng hộ một ý tưởng mới.
hints: The problem your idea solves.
The idea in one sentence.
Benefits and cost.
A small first step to reduce risk.
useful: I'd be happy to lead it
items.opener: I'd like five minutes to share an idea that could save us a lot of time during the salary review.

items.en: Explain a complex HR rule to people who don't work in HR.
items.vi: Giải thích một quy định nhân sự phức tạp cho người ngoài ngành.
hints: Choose one rule, for example how tax on bonuses works.
Avoid jargon or explain it simply.
Use a simple example with round numbers.
Check understanding.
items.opener: Let me explain this without any technical words.

items.en: Handle a question you can't answer in a meeting.
items.vi: Xử lý câu hỏi mà bạn chưa trả lời được trong cuộc họp.
hints: Thank the person for the question.
Be honest that you don't know yet.
Share what you do know.
Promise a follow-up with a time.
useful: I don't have the exact figure
what I can tell you is
let me check and come back to you
items.opener: That's a great question, and I want to give you an accurate answer.

items.en: Propose a solution to a problem that keeps happening in your team.
items.vi: Đề xuất giải pháp cho một vấn đề lặp lại trong nhóm.
hints: Describe the problem and how often it happens.
Explain the root cause.
Propose a solution.
Explain how you'll measure success.
useful: let's try it for a month
items.opener: Every month, we face the same problem with late timesheets.

items.en: Present the pros and cons of a four-day work week.
items.vi: Trình bày ưu và nhược điểm của tuần làm 4 ngày.
hints: Pros: well-being, attraction and productivity.
Cons: customer coverage and higher pressure on four days.
Which roles it could work for.
Your conclusion.
items.opener: A four-day work week sounds great, but is it realistic for a company like ours?

items.en: Open an online meeting with a regional team.
items.vi: Mở đầu cuộc họp online với nhóm khu vực.
hints: Greet people in different locations and time zones.
Check the audio and screen sharing.
State the goal of the call.
Explain how people can ask questions.
useful: good morning or good afternoon, depending on where you are
the goal of today's call is
feel free to use the chat
items.opener: Good morning or good afternoon, everyone, depending on where you are.

items.en: Explain why a project is delayed and what you will do.
items.vi: Giải thích vì sao dự án bị chậm và bạn sẽ làm gì.
hints: State the delay clearly.
Explain the reason without blaming people.
Present the new plan.
Say what you need from others.
useful: I need to let you know that
items.opener: I need to be upfront with you: the job evaluation project is running about two weeks late.

items.en: Tell me about yourself.
items.vi: Hãy giới thiệu về bản thân.
hints: Your current role and experience in a few words.
One or two key achievements.
What you're looking for next.
Keep it to about one minute.
useful: I have ... years of experience in
one thing I'm proud of is
items.opener: I'm a C&B specialist with six years of experience, mostly in manufacturing.

items.en: Why do you want to work in compensation and benefits?
items.vi: Vì sao bạn muốn làm mảng lương thưởng – phúc lợi?
hints: What first got you interested.
What you enjoy about the work.
How it uses your strengths.
What you want to achieve.
useful: I'd like to make a difference
items.opener: I like C&B because it sits where numbers and people meet.

items.en: What is your greatest strength?
items.vi: Điểm mạnh lớn nhất của bạn là gì?
hints: Name one strength.
Give a specific example.
Show the result.
Link it to the job.
useful: in this role, it would help me
items.opener: I'd say my greatest strength is attention to detail.

items.en: What is an area you're working to improve?
items.vi: Bạn đang cải thiện điểm nào?
hints: Be honest and choose something real but not critical.
Explain how you noticed it.
Describe what you're doing about it.
Show your progress.
useful: it's still a work in progress
items.opener: One area I'm actively working on is speaking up in large meetings.

items.en: Tell me about a time you worked under a lot of pressure.
items.vi: Kể về một lần bạn làm việc dưới áp lực lớn.
hints: Situation: what made it stressful.
Task: what you needed to deliver.
Action: how you organised yourself.
Result: what happened in the end.
items.opener: During my first year-end payroll, three people in my team were off sick at the same time.

items.en: Describe a time you had a conflict with a colleague.
items.vi: Kể về một lần bạn mâu thuẫn với đồng nghiệp.
hints: What the disagreement was about.
How you approached the conversation.
How you reached an agreement.
What the relationship is like now.
items.opener: I once disagreed with a finance colleague about how to forecast the bonus pool.

items.en: Tell me about a time you used data to influence a decision.
items.vi: Kể về lần bạn dùng dữ liệu để tác động đến quyết định.
hints: The decision and who made it.
The data you collected and analysed.
How you presented it.
The decision that was made and its impact.
items.opener: Management was about to cut the merit budget, and I used turnover data to change their minds.

items.en: Why should we hire you?
items.vi: Vì sao chúng tôi nên tuyển bạn?
hints: Match your experience to the main needs of the role.
Mention one thing that makes you different.
Show motivation.
Finish confidently.
items.opener: From what you've told me, you need someone who can fix the structure and explain it clearly.

items.en: Why are you leaving your current job?
items.vi: Vì sao bạn rời công việc hiện tại?
hints: Stay positive about your current employer.
Focus on what you're looking for, not what you're escaping.
Mention growth and new challenges.
Link it to this role.
useful: the next step in my career
items.opener: I've had a great four years at my current company, and I've learned a lot there.

items.en: Describe a process you improved.
items.vi: Mô tả một quy trình bạn đã cải tiến.
hints: What the old process was and its problem.
What you changed.
How you got others to accept the change.
The measurable result.
items.opener: Our old salary review process used twenty different Excel files.

items.en: How do you keep up with changes in labour law and the market?
items.vi: Bạn cập nhật thay đổi luật lao động và thị trường thế nào?
hints: Official sources you follow.
Networks and events.
Surveys and reports.
How you share updates with your team.
items.opener: In C&B, rules change every year, so staying up to date is part of the job.

items.en: How do you handle confidential information?
items.vi: Bạn xử lý thông tin bảo mật thế nào?
hints: Why confidentiality matters in C&B.
Practical steps: access rights, passwords, clean desk.
What you do when someone asks about others' pay.
An example.
items.opener: In C&B, we see everyone's salary, so confidentiality is not optional.

items.en: Tell me about a time you failed.
items.vi: Kể về một lần bạn thất bại.
hints: Choose a real failure with a clear lesson.
Take responsibility.
What you learned.
How you've applied it since.
items.opener: A few years ago, I launched a recognition programme that almost nobody used.

items.en: Describe your ideal manager.
items.vi: Mô tả người quản lý lý tưởng của bạn.
hints: Two or three qualities.
Why they matter to you.
How you work best.
Keep it positive.
items.opener: I work best with a manager who gives clear goals and then trusts me to deliver.

items.en: Respond to a job offer that is lower than you expected.
items.vi: Phản hồi một lời mời làm việc thấp hơn kỳ vọng.
hints: Thank them and show interest.
State the gap politely.
Support your request with data or experience.
Ask about flexibility in other parts of the package.
useful: I was expecting something closer to
I'm confident we can find a solution
items.opener: Thank you so much for the offer. I'm really excited about the role.

items.en: Ask your manager for a promotion.
items.vi: Đề nghị quản lý xét thăng chức.
hints: Describe how your role has grown.
Give two or three results.
Show you're already working at the next level.
Ask for a clear next step and timeline.
useful: I'd like to be considered for
what would I need to show
items.opener: I'd like to talk about my next step in the team.

items.en: Negotiate a later start date with a new employer.
items.vi: Thương lượng lùi ngày bắt đầu với công ty mới.
hints: Thank them and confirm you're committed.
Explain your notice period or reason.
Suggest a specific date.
Offer something in return, like joining an onboarding call early.
useful: would it be possible to start on
items.opener: I'm really looking forward to joining, and I want to leave my current job properly.

items.en: Explain to a candidate why the offer can't go higher.
items.vi: Giải thích cho ứng viên vì sao lời mời không thể cao hơn.
hints: Show that you understand their request.
Explain the range and internal equity.
Highlight the rest of the package.
Offer a future review or other options.
useful: to keep it fair for the team
items.opener: I understand you were hoping for more, and I want to be transparent about why we can't go higher.

items.en: Ask for flexible working arrangements.
items.vi: Đề nghị chế độ làm việc linh hoạt.
hints: What you're asking for exactly.
Why it matters to you.
How you'll make sure the work still gets done.
Suggest a trial period.
items.opener: I'd like to ask about the possibility of working from home two days a week.

items.en: As an employer, respond to a competing offer.
items.vi: Là nhà tuyển dụng, phản hồi lời mời cạnh tranh của ứng viên.
hints: Thank the candidate for being open.
Ask what matters most to them.
Compare the whole package, not only base pay.
Make a clear and final proposal.
useful: this is our best and final offer
items.opener: Thank you for telling me about the other offer; I appreciate your honesty.

items.en: Negotiate a better price with a salary survey vendor.
items.vi: Thương lượng giá tốt hơn với nhà cung cấp khảo sát lương.
hints: Explain your budget limit.
Mention your long relationship or a multi-year deal.
Ask for options: smaller scope or a discount.
Agree on next steps in writing.
useful: if we commit to two years
items.opener: We'd really like to continue working with you, but this year's budget is tight.

items.en: Ask your manager for a training budget.
items.vi: Đề nghị quản lý cấp ngân sách đào tạo.
hints: The course and its cost.
How it helps your work and the team.
How you'll share what you learn.
When you'd like to start.
useful: I'd like to take a course in
I can share what I learn
items.opener: I've found a course that I think would really help our team.

items.en: How do you write an email explaining a payroll error to employees?
items.vi: Bạn viết email giải thích lỗi tính lương cho nhân viên thế nào?
hints: A clear subject line.
Apologise and explain what happened, briefly.
Say what will be corrected and when.
Give a contact for questions.
useful: I'd start with a clear subject line
the correction will be paid on
no action is needed from you
items.opener: When there's a payroll error, the email needs to be short, honest and very clear.

items.en: What makes a good work email?
items.vi: Thế nào là một email công việc tốt?
hints: A subject that says what it's about.
The main point in the first two lines.
Short paragraphs or bullet points.
A clear request and deadline.
items.opener: For me, a good email is one that people can understand in thirty seconds.

items.en: How do you follow up politely when someone doesn't reply?
items.vi: Bạn nhắc lại lịch sự thế nào khi ai đó chưa trả lời?
hints: Wait a reasonable time.
Write a short, friendly reminder.
Repeat the key request and deadline.
If there's still no reply, call or talk in person.
useful: could you let me know by
I try not to sound pushy
items.opener: Following up is a big part of my job, because I depend on data from many people.
